findings.comment: Sheet 21 references an 'Electrical Vault Easement' but the transformer within it is labeled as a 'pad.' Clarify whether the transformer is pad-mounted (compliant) or installed in a subsurface vault (non-compliant outside Network Area per UCM § 1.5.2.6). If a vault installation is proposed outside the Network Area, reconfigure to either: (a) pad-mounted transformer (clear to sky), or (b) specialized niche meeting UCM § 1.10.4 footnote 3 requirements (35-foot vertical clearance, 3-hour fire-rated walls/ceilings, exterior access, proper ventilation, truck accessibility).
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) visual analysis identified the presence of an 'Electrical Vault Easement' labeled near the southwest entrance of the site. The vision analysis noted this easement 'encompasses a transformer pad and pull box.' The site is located at 3759 Valley View Road, Austin TX 78704 in the MF-2 zoning district, which is not part of the downtown Network Area (UCM § 1.11.5). No Network Area service is indicated on the site plans. The term 'vault easement' is used in the labeling, but the transformer within it is described as a 'pad' (pad-mounted), which typically refers to aboveground equipment. However, the use of the term 'vault' in the easement designation creates ambiguity as to whether the transformer is truly a subsurface vault installation or simply an easement area serving a pad-mounted transformer.
findings.reasoning: EL-19.22 specifies 'Vaults or meter rooms proposed outside Network Area where vaults are not permitted' and applies only when 'vaults or subsurface/enclosed transformer rooms are proposed.' UCM § 1.5.2.6 restricts transformer vaults to the Network Area only; outside the Network Area, transformers must be pad-mounted (clear to sky) or installed in specialized niches meeting specific requirements (UCM § 1.10.4 footnote 3). The site is clearly outside the Network Area. The ambiguity arises from the sheet's reference to an 'Electrical Vault Easement' while the transformer within it is labeled as a 'pad.' This terminology conflict must be clarified: if the transformer is truly installed in a subsurface vault, it violates UCM § 1.5.2.6. If it is a pad-mounted transformer within an easement area, it is compliant. The preliminary nature of the electrical plan and lack of detailed transformer installation specifications (normal pad-mounted vs. vault vs. niche configuration) prevent a definitive determination.

findings.comment: Transformer installation method and site location relative to Network Area require clarification. Confirm whether proposed installation near Building 8 is pad-mounted or vaulted. If vaulted, verify site location against Network Area Map (UCM § 1.11.5); vaults are permitted exclusively within Network Area. If outside Network Area and vault is proposed, verify specialized niche meeting UCM § 1.10.4 footnote 3 requirements (35-foot vertical clearance, 3-hour fire-rated walls, accessible from outside, proper ventilation, truck accessibility). Clarify 'Vault Easement' designation on electrical site plan.
applicableAreas: transformer installation near Building 8 (southwest portion of site)
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows four transformer pads labeled as 'Electrical Transformer Pad' (indicating pad-mount configuration per vision analysis). However, near Building 8 in the southwestern area, the plan also includes a label for 'Vault Easement,' which raises the question of whether a vault installation is being proposed in addition to or instead of a pad-mount transformer. Vision analysis of Sheet 21 notes this explicit 'Vault Easement' label in the bottom right area near the Bldg 8 transformer location. UCM § 1.5.2.6 restricts transformer vaults to the Network Area only; vaults outside the Network Area are not permitted (vaults are only permitted exclusively within the Network Area boundaries per grouping narrative). The preliminary electrical site plan does not explicitly state whether a vault is proposed or whether the 'Vault Easement' is simply a property easement designation. The grouping narrative states that 'Network area determination requires cross-referencing the project address against the official Network Area Map at https://mcclibrary.blob.core.usgovcloudapi.net/codecontent/15312/483105/1-11-5.png, as this cannot be determined from site plans alone.' Thus, from the site plan alone, it cannot be confirmed: (1) whether a vault is actually being proposed, or (2) whether the site is within Network Area boundaries.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.5.2.6 states that transformer vaults are permitted exclusively within the Network Area boundaries. If the site is outside the Network Area and a vault is being proposed, this violates the requirement. The vision analysis found an explicit 'Vault Easement' labeled on Sheet 21, which suggests that some kind of vaulted or enclosed transformer installation may be planned. However, the same sheet labels transformers as 'Electrical Transformer Pad' (pad-mount). The ambiguity between the vault easement designation and the pad-mount labels, combined with the inability to verify Network Area status from site plans alone (per grouping instruction), creates an unclear status. If a vault is proposed outside the Network Area, this would be a clear violation; if only pad-mount installations are proposed, the vault easement may be a property easement that does not trigger this deficiency. The preliminary design stage may also explain the ambiguity.

findings.comment: Verify the site location relative to the Austin Energy Network Area Map (UCM § 1.11.5) at https://mcclibrary.blob.core.usgovcloudapi.com/codecontent/15312/483105/1-11-5.png. If the site is within the Network Area, confirm transformer installation is vault-type per UCM § 1.5.2.6. If outside the Network Area, confirm transformers are pad-mounted (as shown) or, if enclosed, demonstrate they meet specialized niche requirements: 35-foot vertical clearance, 3-hour fire-rated walls/ceilings, accessible from outside the building, proper ventilation, and truck accessibility per UCM § 1.10.4 footnote 3.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows four 'Electrical Transformer Pad' locations depicted as rectangular symbols. These appear to be pad-mounted transformers (clear-to-sky installation), not subsurface vaults or enclosed transformer rooms. The grouping states 'Only when vaults or subsurface/enclosed transformer rooms are proposed' and requires applicability assessment. UCM § 1.5.2.6 states 'Transformer Installation Requirements (vaults restricted to Network Area).' Pad-mounted transformers are permissible outside the Network Area. However, the Network Area status of the site at 3759 Valley View Road, Austin TX 78704 has not been verified from site plans or in the documentation. Without Network Area determination, and given that the transformers shown are pad-mounted (not vaults), this item appears to have limited applicability. However, if a vault installation were proposed, Network Area confirmation would be critical.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.5.2.6 restricts transformer vaults exclusively to the Network Area. Outside the Network Area, only pad-mounted (clear-to-sky) transformers or specialized niches meeting specific requirements (35-foot vertical clearance, 3-hour fire-rated walls, accessible from outside, proper ventilation, truck accessibility per UCM § 1.10.4 footnote 3) are permitted. The site plan shows pad-mounted transformers, which are compliant outside the Network Area. The Network Area determination cannot be verified from site plans. If the site is actually within the Network Area and the transformers should be vaults instead, or if specialized niches are being proposed, this would need verification. Without the Network Area map cross-reference, definitive assessment is unclear.

findings.comment: Vault Easement notation appears on electrical plan for property outside downtown Network Area. Clarify whether transformer vault rooms (subsurface rooms) are proposed; if so, provide evidence that site is within the downtown Network Area per UCM § 1.11.5. If site is outside Network Area (as facts indicate), transformer vaults are prohibited; transformers must be pad-mounted or in niches with AE Design consultation per UCM § 1.5.2.6.
applicableAreas: Transformer locations and proposed service configuration
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) showing four transformer pads labeled as "Electrical Transformer Pad". The property is located at 3759 Valley View Road, Austin, TX 78704, which is in South Austin. According to facts.md, there is no Network Area designation at this property and no regulating plan applies. The Network Area is defined in UCM § 1.11.5 as the downtown Austin area providing vault-only service. The site location is outside downtown and the project facts confirm no Network Area status. However, Sheet 21 shows one transformer location with an adjacent "Vault Easement" label, suggesting a possible vault configuration may be planned. If transformer vaults are being proposed at this location outside the Network Area, this would violate code requirements (UCM § 1.5.2.6 and § 1.10.4 require vault-only service in Network Area; outside Network Area, transformers must be pad-mounted or in niches per UCM § 1.5.2.6).
findings.reasoning: Code limits transformer vault rooms to the downtown Network Area only (UCM § 1.5.2.6 and § 1.11.5). Outside the Network Area, transformers must be pad-mounted or located in niches (with AE Design consultation). The site is clearly outside the Network Area (South Lamar area, no Network Area designation per facts.md). The presence of a "Vault Easement" label on Sheet 21 near Building 2 raises the question of whether a transformer vault room (subsurface room with multiple transformers) is being proposed outside the Network Area. If the vault easement indicates a planned vault room (rather than just vault infrastructure within a padmount config), this would be a code violation. Clarification is needed about the exact nature of the vault easement and whether transformer vault rooms are being proposed.

findings.comment: Sheet 21 shows a 'Vault Easement' notation adjacent to Transformer 4, indicating proposed vault infrastructure. The property is located outside the downtown Network Area (UCM § 1.11.5) where vault rooms are prohibited. Transformers outside the Network Area must be pad-mounted or in niches with AE Design consultation. Clarify: (1) Remove the Vault Easement notation if transformers will be pad-mounted, or (2) If a vault is intended, this site does not qualify per UCM § 1.5.2.6 and § 1.11.5 and cannot proceed with vault design at this location.
applicableAreas: Transformer pad 4 (southwestern side, west of Bldg. 8) and vicinity
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) which shows Transformer 4 in the southwestern portion of the site (west of Bldg. 8). Vision analysis of this sheet identified that 'immediately adjacent to this pad is a dashed rectangle labeled "Vault Easement", suggesting below-grade infrastructure may be associated with this specific location.' The notation of a 'Vault Easement' indicates the applicant intends or is planning for vault infrastructure at this location. Per facts.md, the property address (3759 Valley View Road, Austin, TX 78704) is in South Austin, MF-2 zoning, and there is NO notation of the site being in the 'Network Area.' The facts.md specifically confirms: 'Regulating Plan: None' and the site address and zoning clearly place this property outside the downtown Network Area defined in UCM § 1.11.5.
findings.reasoning: The notation of 'Vault Easement' adjacent to Transformer 4 indicates an intent to construct or provide access to underground vault infrastructure. Per UCM § 1.5.2.6 and § 1.11.5, transformer vault rooms are only permitted within the downtown Network Area. The property is clearly outside the Network Area (South Austin location, Valley View Road, MF-2 zoning). Therefore, vault room construction is prohibited at this location. The applicant must either: (1) remove the vault easement notation and confirm all transformers are pad-mounted only, or (2) if a vault is intended, relocate the infrastructure to a property within the downtown Network Area.

findings.comment: Austin Water fire demand meter vault (8' x 12' structure shown on Sheet 20) is depicted on the utility tap plan, but no exclusive 5-foot space around and under the vault is documented on the plans. Provide dimension callouts or notes on the utility plan confirming that the vault maintains the required 5-foot exclusive space with no other utilities or structures encroaching within this zone.
applicableAreas: Fire demand meter vault area and surrounding utility infrastructure
findings.observation: Sheet 20 (Utility Tap Public Plan & Profile) identifies a structure labeled '8' Fire Demand Meter in 8' x 12' Vault' on the plan view west of the property entrance. The vault is shown with its footprint on the plan and appears to connect to the proposed water line at the tap location. Sheet 19 shows various utilities (water, wastewater, electrical) routed through the site in proximity to this vault area. However, no plan view or detail on either sheet documents or verifies that an exclusive 5-foot space exists around and under the vault structure, free of other underground utilities, appurtenances, or structures. UCM § 2.9.1.A.4 requires Austin Water vaults to maintain 5-foot exclusive space around and under the vault; no plan notation, dimension callout, or specification confirms that this requirement has been addressed or verified.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 2.9.1.A.4 requires that Austin Water vaults maintain required 5-foot exclusive space around and under the vault structure, with no other underground utilities, appurtenances, or structures allowed to encroach within this zone. The vault location is identified on the plan, and its general footprint is shown, but the plans provide no documentation that this exclusive space requirement has been verified or is being provided. Without dimension callouts or notes showing the 5-foot exclusion zone and confirming that no other utilities encroach within it, compliance cannot be confirmed from the available plan documentation. This is unclear because the plans lack sufficient information to verify the exclusive space requirement.

findings.comment: No electrical engineering load calculations, transformer specifications, or ESPA form reference are provided on Sheet 21 or in supplementary documents. Provide: (1) Complete electrical engineering calculations including transformer count, kVA ratings, voltage classes, and amperage specifications for all proposed transformers, (2) ESPA (Electrical System Project Application) form completed and submitted to Austin Energy Network Design, (3) Final voltage and load documentation confirming the proposed equipment meets the development's power requirements and complies with Austin Energy standards.
applicableAreas: Transformer equipment specifications and vault design (if applicable)
findings.observation: Reviewed Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) and the Engineer's Summary Letter supplementary document. Block 3 of Sheet 21 drawing shows 'electrical elements such as transformers, pull boxes, underground electric lines, and electrical meters' but provides no equipment specifications. The blocks.md for Sheet 21 explicitly states: 'None are provided on this sheet. The items are generically labeled Electrical Transformer Pad.' No electrical engineering report, load calculations, transformer kVA ratings, voltage specifications, phase information, or ESPA (Electrical System Project Application) form references are provided in any of the submitted documents. The Engineer's Summary Letter (supplementary doc) addresses only water and wastewater utilities, with no mention of electrical load calculations or transformer specifications. No transformer count is documented anywhere on the submitted plans.
findings.reasoning: Without load calculations and transformer specifications, Austin Energy Design and Network Design cannot verify that the proposed electrical infrastructure is adequate for the development's power requirements. The design is incomplete per UCM § 1.11.1 and cannot proceed to construction without this essential information.

findings.comment: Transformer vault is referenced by 'Vault Easement' label on electrical plan, but no vault design specifications or evidence of AE Network Design approval is provided. If transformer vault service is proposed, provide complete vault design including interior dimensions, access specifications, fire ratings, ventilation details, load calculations, and documented AE Network Design approval. If vault is not proposed, clarify the purpose of the vault easement notation.
applicableAreas: Transformer locations near Building 2 with nearby 'Vault Easement' label
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan). Near Building 2, one of the four transformer pad locations is accompanied by a text label reading "Vault Easement" pointing to a dashed rectangular boundary area that also contains an "Electrical Pull Box" label. This label indicates the presence of a vault easement in that location. However, no vault design details are shown on this sheet or any other electrical, grading, or site plan sheet in the available documentation. There are no vault door specifications, vault interior dimensions, access details, fire rating notes, ventilation provisions, or any other vault-specific design information visible.
findings.reasoning: Code requires transformer vaults to be submitted to AE Network Design for approval, and vault location, access, and elevation must be coordinated with AE Network Design (allow 3-6 months for vault design review per UCM § 1.11.1.D). The presence of a "Vault Easement" label suggests a subsurface vault may be planned, but the preliminary electrical plan provides no vault design documentation or AE Network Design coordination evidence. If a transformer vault is being planned (indicated by the easement), it should be accompanied by detailed vault design, load calculations, fire rating specifications, and documented AE Network Design approval. The lack of vault design details alongside the easement label creates ambiguity about whether a vault is actually planned or if this is merely an easement designation.

findings.comment: Cannot verify vault requirements from available evidence. Provide Austin Energy Design documentation (ESPA approval, Letter of Agreement, or utility coordination notes) confirming the approved service type (pad-mounted transformer, vault, or specialized niche). If pad-mounted transformers are approved, verify compliance with UCM § 1.10.4 clearance requirements per UCM § 1.5.1.6.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows transformer pads (5 total) but no indication of vault structures. The facts.md indicates the site is located in Austin, TX but does NOT place it within the Downtown Network Area per facts.md statement "Regulating Plan: None". UCM § 1.11.5 defines the Network Area boundaries where vaults are permitted. The applicability note in the checklist states vaults are required only "Inside Network Area: vaults required for services above 800 amps. Outside Network Area: vaults generally not permitted - only pad-mounted transformers or specialized niches." The site appears to be outside the Network Area, suggesting pad-mounted transformers (which are shown) would be the appropriate service type. However, without formal Austin Energy Design documentation confirming the service type decision and demonstrating compliance with UCM § 1.10.4 (Clearances from AE Padmount Equipment) if pedestals/niches are used, the determination cannot be conclusively verified.
findings.reasoning: The determination of whether vaults are required cannot be made from site plan features alone - it requires (1) confirmation of location relative to Network Area boundaries, and (2) Austin Energy Design documentation confirming the approved service type. While the site appears to be outside the Network Area (suggesting pad-mounted transformers are appropriate), formal AE Design documentation is required to verify this determination. The absence of such documentation means the applicant's choice of pad-mounted transformers cannot be verified as AE-approved.
